review_notes:
I read all 85 lines of the target file and checked whether any non-trivial argument appears in two or more proofs. Each proof uses a different argument:
- `closedUpperDisk_eq` uses `ext` and `simp`.
- `closedUpperDisk_isClosed` and `openUpperDisk_isOpen` are short one-term `isClosed_le`/`isOpen_lt` combinations. They have the same shape, but each is a thin use of existing API, so the rubric excludes them.
- `closedUpperDisk_convex` takes a convex intersection.
- `closedUpperDisk_interior` rewrites with `interior_inter`, `interior_closedBall` and `imCLM.interior_preimage`.
- `openUpperDisk_convex` and `openUpperDisk_closure` follow from the convex-interior lemmas.
- `openUpperDisk_frontier` is the only longer proof, and it is a single case split on the set difference.
- `complexInside_upperDisk` makes one call to `complexInside_eq_open` plus one boundedness check.

I also looked for related machinery in sibling files under `lean/OAI/Probability/SLE`. `DiskBoundaryRegion.lean` defines the lower half disk. It does not repeat these closure, interior or frontier arguments: it carries the upper-disk results over to the lower disk through complex conjugation (`conjCLE.toHomeomorph`, `complexInside_transport`). The only other caller of `complexInside_eq_open`, `complexInside_unitDisk`, is a short application with different inputs. So no shared helper lemma would clearly improve this file. The remaining uncertainty is small: I did not exhaustively search the whole repository for other files that might rebuild half-disk interiors or frontiers from scratch.
